question: Summarize the results of the Rivertown bike-share pilot.

claims.claim: The Rivertown bike-share pilot ran for six months, starting in March 2025.
claims.note: 1 March to 31 August 2025.

claims.claim: It deployed 400 bicycles across 25 docking stations.
The pilot cost INR 4.2 crore.
claims.note: Report says INR 2.4 crore (digits swapped).

claims.claim: More than twelve thousand people signed up as registered users.
claims.note: 12,500 registered; wording differs, must NOT be flagged.

claims.claim: Riders made 186,000 trips in total.
claims.note: Also in the monthly table total.

claims.claim: The average trip lasted 25 minutes.
claims.note: Report says 18 minutes.

claims.claim: Central Station was the busiest location, accounting for 14% of all trips.
claims.note: Stated in text and Table 2.

claims.claim: Most trips took place on weekdays.
claims.note: Weekday trips were 71%.

claims.claim: With 186,000 trips and 400 bicycles, each bicycle averaged roughly 465 trips over the pilot.
The pilot attracted 12,500 users, 62% of whom were commuters.
claims.note: 12,500 is users (p2) but 62% refers to trips, not users (p3).

claims.claim: Cycling is good for cardiovascular health.
claims.note: True in real life but absent from the PDF: must be Insufficient, NOT Contradicted.

claims.claim: The program was most popular among university students.
claims.note: PDF gives no user demographics.

claims.claim: 37 bicycles were stolen.
Only 12 bicycles were damaged.
claims.note: Report says 112 damaged.

claims.claim: Maintenance crews responded within one hour on average.
claims.note: Report says an average of 6 hours.

claims.claim: Since 78% of surveyed users were satisfied, the pilot significantly reduced traffic congestion.
claims.note: Satisfaction (p6) does not imply congestion reduction; congestion was not assessed (p8).

claims.claim: Many users asked for night-time availability.
claims.note: Report says 'several users'; 'many' is vague, should not be hard-labelled false.

claims.claim: The report did not measure the effect on air quality.
claims.note: Report states air quality was not assessed.

claims.claim: The city council has already approved expanding to 40 stations.
claims.note: Report: subject to approval, no decision made yet.

claims.claim: Because damaged bicycles were rare, riders can safely skip pre-ride inspections.
claims.note: 112 bikes were damaged and riders are asked to check brakes and tyres.

claims.claim: The report was prepared in September 2025.
claims.note: Cover page.

claims.claim: Harbour Road was the second busiest station, with 18,600 trips.
claims.note: Table 2.

claims.claim: The five busiest stations handled 48% of all trips.
Fare revenue covered about 13% of the pilot's cost.
Helmets were supplied with every bicycle.
claims.note: Report: helmets were not supplied.

claims.claim: No serious injuries were reported during the pilot.
The pilot was run entirely by the municipal office without any contractor.
claims.note: Operations were handled by CycleWorks Ltd.

claims.claim: The most common complaint was bicycle availability during peak hours.
claims.note: 31% of respondents.

claims.claim: The findings show that a full year of operation would give similar results.
claims.note: Report says seasonal effects over a full year are not known.

claims.claim: Fare revenue was low.
claims.note: INR 0.31 crore of INR 2.4 crore: 'low' is a judgement, not stated.
